rows.basis: The Q4 2024 release states full-year 2024 Enterprise Data revenue of $716.2M. That is 716.2M ÷ 2,207.1M = 32.5%, matching the stated 32.5% share. Enterprise Data is MPS's data-center power line and includes non-AI server parts, so this is an upper bound on AI revenue.

The pack has no full-year 2025 Enterprise Data figure, only quarterly amounts (Q2 $144.0M, Q3 $191.5M), so the year cannot be summed. Releases attribute sequential growth to 'power management solutions for AI and server applications'. The thesis cites full-year Enterprise Data of $701.8M (25.2% of revenue, down 2.0%), but no pack item states it.

The FY2023 MD&A attributes the revenue increase 'primarily' to 'higher sales of our power management solutions for AI applications'. The pack has no full-year Enterprise Data amount for 2023; the 10.9% share refers to Q2 2023 only. The FY2024 release puts 2023 Enterprise Data at 17.7% of revenue, but that statement's pack share is the 2024 figure.
MPS states no AI amount or share of its own capex ($58.8M). A chip seller's capex funds production equipment, test and facilities, not AI infrastructure.

MPS states no AI amount or share of its own capex ($57.6M); it funds production and test, not AI infrastructure. Seller-side signal: FY2023 revenue growth was attributed to AI power management sales (MD&A).

MPS states no AI amount or share of its own capex ($146.1M); it funds production equipment and facilities, not AI infrastructure. Seller-side signal: Enterprise Data revenue was $716.2M in 2024, recorded as the revenue row.

MPS states no AI amount or share of its own capex ($172.0M); it funds production equipment and construction, not AI infrastructure. Seller-side signal: Enterprise Data was $701.8M in 2025 per the thesis (Q4 2025 release), down 2.0%.
